FINDING A1 — P2: Historical source deduplication makes a reverted draft impossible to submit for review
Location: backend/src/main/java/com/ticknova/knowledge/KnowledgeService.java:142-144; related current-version gate :188 and :202; db/migration/V5__knowledge_authoring_review.sql:40-43.
Reproduction path (deterministic source trace; not executed by reviewer): create an article with fixed title/category and content A, commit it as v1 and let parsing finish without reviewing it. Save content B and commit v2. Then save the same title/category and content A again and commit using a fresh Idempotency-Key. persistUpload searches every non-REJECTED version and returns v1 from the early return. It does not reach the latest_version_id update at line 154, so latest_version_id remains v2. Requesting review for the successful commit result v1 returns 409 VERSION_NOT_READY because v1 is not latest. If v1 was already PENDING when v2 was created, the analogous review endpoint rejects it as non-current. Repeated commits of A continue to return v1. The same mismatch affects file-version reversion.
Actual consequence: a normal undo/revert workflow reports a successful committed upload but cannot proceed through the mandatory current-version review workflow. The UI flags likewise leave v1 without the required review action. An editor must change the content/metadata artificially to escape the dead end.
Suggested fix: reconcile snapshot deduplication with the current-version invariant. Reusing a historical DRAFT/PENDING snapshot must either atomically make that snapshot the current editable version under the existing locks, or create a new eligible revision with appropriately revised uniqueness rules. Keep exact current-version duplicate uploads/idempotent replays deduplicated, retain immutable source and existing publication, and add an A -> B -> A regression proving that the returned version can proceed through independent review/publication. A query-only change to deduplicate latest versions is insufficient unless the cross-history unique indexes are also reconciled.

FINDING A2 — P2: Inline code is escaped as prose before serialization, changing the source text
Location: backend/src/main/java/com/ticknova/knowledge/RichDocument.java:89-91.
Reproduction path (deterministic source trace; not executed by reviewer): submit a valid RichDoc paragraph containing text "a < b && x_y" with a code mark, then commit it. renderText first calls escape(), giving "a < b && x\_y", and then places that escaped value inside a Markdown code span. The serialized source becomes ` a < b && x\_y `. Markdown code spans retain these entities/backslashes literally; they do not apply prose entity or backslash decoding. Windows paths and punctuation such as asterisks have the same corruption. With multiple permitted marks, previously added Markdown emphasis delimiters can also become literal code contents depending on mark order.
Actual consequence: the immutable RichDoc reader displays the intended command/expression, while the generated private Markdown sent through Docling and onward to chunks/RAG contains changed code. This violates the required source-format fidelity and can give users incorrect copyable instructions or AI answers even though the rich snapshot/hash checks succeed. Existing RichDocumentTest covers escaped prose and links, but no inline-code source fidelity test.
Suggested fix: serialize code spans from the raw normalized text with a delimiter/padding strategy valid for embedded backticks; apply any compatible outer marks outside the code span in a canonical order, or normalize unsupported combinations explicitly. Do not run prose HTML/backslash escaping inside code spans. Add focused cases for <, &, _, *, backslashes, embedded backticks, and combined marks, plus a generated-article parser/source round-trip assertion where supported. Maintain the closed safe RichDoc schema and no executable HTML rendering.
